This triggers the phishing checklist (potential typo-squatted domain and unexpected email). For safety, do NOT click the 'Claim Your Refund' link. Recommended next steps: (1) Verify by signing into your Amazon account directly (not via the email) and check order/refund history; (2) If you believe it's fraudulent, forward the message to Amazon at stop-spoofing@amazon.com and then delete it; (3) If you have concerns about charges, contact Amazon Customer Service from the official site or your account page. I returned to the inbox and ended the task to avoid following a potentially malicious link.
